findings.observation: Contributor GitHub docs contradict the live main ruleset: they claim direct merges to main are allowed and treat checks-complete as the merge wall, while governance and CI require pr-gate-complete and block direct pushes.
findings.method: Inspection of contributor docs vs docs/00-project/governance/05-github-policy.md and .github/workflows/pr-required.yml
findings.expected: Contributor docs MUST match RULES.md §6 (required checks / contributor sync) and the live ruleset: no direct push to main; GitHub-required context is pr-gate-complete.
findings.actual: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md:120-122 says direct merges to main are allowed and branch protection is not enforcing checks. github-quick-reference.md:121 instructs git push origin main --tags. github-local-workflow.md:252-261 lists checks-complete as a main blocking check and omits pr-gate-complete.
findings.impact: Contributors may attempt forbidden pushes to main or wait on the wrong CI job name; PRs can look 'green' locally against stale check names while pr-gate-complete is the real merge wall.
findings.root_cause: Contributor GitHub guidance was not re-synced after ruleset 13643213 / #10267 made pr-gate-complete the required context and blocked direct main updates.
findings.remediation: Rewrite CONTRIBUTING Branch Protection, github-quick-reference CI/Release, and github-local-workflow Required PR checks to match 05-github-policy.md: ruleset 13643213 active, required context pr-gate-complete, no git push origin main. Point release flow to a PR then tag after merge.
findings.automation: Add a docs assertion that contributor pages mention pr-gate-complete and do not claim direct merges to main are allowed.

evidence.observation: Direct merges to `main` are currently allowed. When you open a PR, keep these checks green even though GitHub branch protection is not currently enforcing them:
PR merges and direct pushes to main are blocked by repository ruleset main (13643213); required context is pr-gate-complete.
Release process runs git push origin main --tags.
Job name: pr-gate-complete is the documented GitHub required context.

findings.observation: Keep a Changelog surface is inconsistent: pyproject and README still advertise 6.1.0 (unreleased) while CHANGELOG also has a dated ## [6.1.0] - 2026-03-11 plus a large Unreleased section.
findings.method: Compare CHANGELOG headings, README badge, pyproject.toml version
findings.expected: REQ-GOV-006 / Keep a Changelog: either bump version for Unreleased work after a dated 6.1.0, or do not keep a dated [6.1.0] section alongside Unreleased on the same version.
findings.actual: CHANGELOG.md:8 ## [Unreleased]; CHANGELOG.md:340 ## [6.1.0] - 2026-03-11; pyproject.toml:7 version = 6.1.0; README.md:8 badge version-6.1.0 (unreleased).
findings.impact: Release consumers cannot tell whether 6.1.0 already shipped; Unreleased items are not versioned.
findings.root_cause: Version was not bumped after the dated 6.1.0 changelog section; Unreleased continued to accumulate on the same number.
findings.remediation: Decide whether 6.1.0 already shipped. If yes, bump pyproject for current Unreleased (e.g. 6.2.0) and stop labeling README 6.1.0 unreleased. If 6.1.0 never shipped, fold or relabel the dated [6.1.0] section so it does not look released.
findings.automation: Existing version-consistency check (scripts.engineering.repo check-versions) should fail this dual heading if it does not already.
